Open Day: Saturday 12 September
You are warmly invited to attend an Open Day at Worth. This event gives families an opportunity to find out more about what the School has to offer and how we deliver ‘education with heart and soul’.
Book your place by clicking here.
Your details
Education withHeart & Soul
Catholic - Co-educational - Boarding & Day
A difference of Worth
At Worth we provide a first-rate education and the many achievements of our pupils demonstrate that fact. But we do not just provide education.
We offer education with heart and soul.
How is that? It comes from 1500 years of Benedictine tradition. A tradition that allows us to welcome all, simply because we insist on a community where all children – whatever their gifts – have nothing to hide from and everything to strive for. A community that has family at its heart.
In this respect, we believe that Worth offers a difference that sets us decisively apart. A difference that ignites the extraordinary in every pupil – to benefit each child and our world.
A Personal Exploration
Visitors to Worth often say that there is something intangible about its atmosphere. Its beautiful surroundings are part of that response, but so is the way we see Worth as a school. For us, results go deeper than examination grades.
Academia and results are important, but we also believe that it is through the dual focus on the highest quality education and personal exploration that our pupils are shaped. Worth pupils are encouraged to try new things, to bring their own cultures to life and share in the cultures of others, to look out into the world for inspiration, and inwardly for purpose.
We believe education should seek to form people, both as individuals and as members of a community; it should foster self-awareness, but not as an end in itself; openness to the life of the spirit is one of aspirations we have for our pupils.
Our Benedictine Tradition
St Benedict’s Rule, far from being a sixth-century relic, helps Worth to be true to its educational ideals within a modern and ambitious context. While we embrace what current thinking and technology have to offer schools, we are not drawn to fashionable trends; teaching and learning must still be about the truth, and learning how to distinguish it from the trivial.
An education rooted in values that look beyond the self develops in Worth pupils a sense of their responsibility in the world and in their community, and gives them the balance and humanity that any parent would be proud to see in the child when he or she leaves school.
With every individual valued and every achievement recognised, worth feels like one big family.

Joining Worth
Apply, Join, Succeed
The Worth application process is uniquely personal, designed to ensure that parents make as informed a decision as possible.
Boys and girls join Worth either at ages 11+ (Year 7), at 13+ (Year 9) or at 16+ (Year 12). Worth also admits a small number of pupils at age 15+ (Year 11) into a one-year IGCSE/Pre-IB course.
A few places occasionally become available for boys and girls for admission at age 12+ (Year 8) or at 14+ (Year 10). Late applicants should contact the Admissions department directly.

pageCache.pageTitle: Worth showed me a new perspective on life | Worth School
pageCache.text:
Your details
Worth showed me a new perspective on life
“Worth showed me a new perspective on life focusing not only on performance, but also community, support and values to live by.” This is what one student told us as he reflected on this summer’s excellent IB Diploma results for the School.
In the second of a series of articles looking back on this summer’s impressive Sixth Form results for the School, we spoke to five students about their results, how Worth helped them, their time at the School and their plans for the future.
Worth is one of the UK’s leading schools for the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma, with 20 years’ experience and an excellent record of results, with a 10-year average of 36 points including many achieving more than 40 points, which is equivalent to 4 A* grades at A Level.
Congratulations to all of our 2026 IB Diploma cohort on their results. Please read on to hear what these five students had to say and look out for another A Level case studies story in the next few days.
You may also like to read:
Celebrating A Level success 2026
For more on the Sixth Form at Worth click here.
CHARLES DE QUINNEMAR
Which subjects did you take and what were your results? Maths AA HL 7, Chemistry HL 7, Physics HL 7, English A SL 6, French B SL 7, Economics SL 7, plus the two core points for Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay, so 43 out of 45 in total.
How did you feel when you got your results? Very happy. It’s a strange moment, because two years of work comes down to a few numbers on a screen. I had worked hard towards the goal of having good grades, so it was good to see that pay off. Once I had seen how it had gone, what I mostly felt was gratitude towards the people who helped me get there.
How did Worth help you achieve those results? In two ways. First, the teachers. Classes are small enough that they notice when something hasn’t landed and the follow-up after that is genuinely personal. You get targeted feedback and if it still isn’t clicking you can always go back for extra explanation outside lessons. Second, the boarding house gives you a rhythm. When everyone around you is working through prep, you end up working too. And as Head of House in Rutherford I had other responsibilities on top of my own work, so I learned quickly that putting things off wasn’t an option.
How much have you enjoyed your time at Worth? I loved it. For me it was mainly the friendships and the sense of community. I was a full boarder and often stayed at school over the weekends, so you get to know people in a way you never would if you went home every night. That’s what stays with me, not the exams.
What are you hoping to do next? I’m going to study engineering at KU Leuven. In the Belgian system you don’t choose your specialisation until after the first year, so I’m keeping that open until I know what I enjoy most.
GRACE MARETT
Which subjects did you take and what were your results? I achieved a result of 38 points. I took higher level Maths AI in which I got a 5, Economics and English in which I got a 6. I also took standard level Psychology in which I got a 7, Chemistry in which I got a 6 and German A in which I got 6.
How did you feel when you got your results? I was extremely happy when I got my results especially because I wasn’t expecting these kinds of results.
How did Worth help you achieve those results? The support and encouragement the teachers offered help me to believe that I could achieve those kinds of results. In addition, some teachers also took extra time to answer all my many questions and helped me organise my revision.
How much have you enjoyed your time at Worth? I truly enjoyed my time at Worth whether that was inside or outside the classroom. I particularly enjoyed being part of team sports and the hockey season was one of my highlights at Worth. Worth has offered me many opportunities for which I am extremely grateful. I have made many memories, tried new things and met so many incredible people which I will never forget. Worth has offered me a second home and it will always be a special place which I love to go back to.
What are you hoping to do next? This coming year I decided to do a gap year where I will be working and traveling. Next year I will be studying Psychology, but it is still unclear at which university.
FLORENTIN KRAPP
Which subjects did you take and what were your results? I took Physics, Maths Analysis and Approaches and English B as my Higher Levels, in which I got all 7s. I took Economics, Global Politics and German A as my Standard Levels, in which I got all 6s. This, with two bonus points, brings my total score up to 41.
How did you feel when you got your results? When I got my results, I felt relieved that all the work during the two years of my IB had paid off. I was especially happy that I got 7s in Maths and Physics because these were by far the most difficult subjects that I have taken in the IB, and those were the subjects I spent most of my time studying.
How did Worth help you achieve those results? Worth really helped to achieve good grades through a great community. This includes the competent teachers who were personally engaged in the journey of each student, but also the peers. I think this especially applies in boarding, where you are always surrounded by others who have the same subjects or older pupils who could help you when you had a question.
How much have you enjoyed your time at Worth? I greatly enjoyed my time at Worth, because it offers so much more than a typical school. For me, it was always about trying out something new like rugby, clay shooting or debating, where you always meet new people as well. And for anyone still undecided whether they should do boarding or be a day student, the most fun part of the school day only starts after school finishes. Like playing football on the Astro, going to the gym or beating your mate in a game of tennis.
What are you hoping to do next? At the start of October this year, I will start a bachelor’s course at the Technical University of Munich in Physics.
MILO MIKOREY BARBER
Which subjects did you take and what were your results? I took Maths AI, German B and History at HL, and Biology, English and Business at SL. I achieved 7s in every subject, with a total of 43 points.
How did you feel when you got your results? I was very pleased with my results, which reflected the hard work and dedication I put in over the two years of the IB. They created a very positive note on which to end my experience at Worth.
How did Worth help you achieve those results? The teaching staff at Worth are extremely dedicated and supportive, allowing you to hand in work for feedback consistently and providing valuable insights into your current work. However, teachers at Worth also know when to let you work independently, something that massively helped me study in the way that works best for me and contributed greatly to my exam results. In addition, the house spirit and dedication to sport created an atmosphere that made learning feel less like a chore.
How much have you enjoyed your time at Worth? My time at Worth since Year 11 has been extraordinary and going there was truly one of the best decisions I have ever made. I met a wide range of people and tried many new things. The nature of a boarding school was a great experience, but also a challenge at times, acting as an amazing opportunity for me to grow and become who I am today. I will forever be grateful to all those who contributed to this experience, both staff and students.
What are you hoping to do next? I am currently taking a gap year, working as an EMT in Munich in order to gain valuable practical work experience. I hope to study medicine in the UK or Germany next.
NOAH MOHY ELDIN
Which subjects did you take and what were your results? I took Biology HL, Economics SL, Business HL, Maths IA SL, German A SL and English B HL. I got a 7 in every subject except for Maths and Economics in which I both scored a 6. I achieved an overall score of 42.
How did you feel when you got your results? I was incredibly relieved when I saw my results and overcome with immense joy, because my results enabled me to pursue my dream career in Germany. It was also very pleasing to see that all the hard work and the long hours I had to put in the last two years were worth it and overall I was very pleased with my results.
How did Worth help you achieve those results? Worth helped me to discover my own strengths and they did this by offering a huge amount of support. The teachers were always there for any academic problem I had and always invested a lot of time and patience in order to help me get my head around it. Additionally, the whole setting at Worth, especially the community and the work ethic of everyone around me encouraged me to go to greater lengths in order to achieve a good result. I was immersed in a community of support, motivation and, last but not least, a lot of empathy towards any type of problem, whether it be academic or of another nature.
How much have you enjoyed your time at Worth? I think it is safe to say that my three years at Worth have not only been the most enjoyable years of my life, they have also been the most eventful and interesting years of my life. Worth showed me a new perspective on life focusing not only on performance, but also community, support and values to live by. Worth not only enables their students to grow strong relationships, but it also enables them to discover their own potential and grow to be better versions of themselves every day.
What are you hoping to do next? I am going to the Ludwig-Maximilians University in Munich to start studying Medicine from October 2026 onwards.

Your details
Families enjoy Open Day at Worth
Worth was delighted to host a hugely successful Open Day on Saturday when more than 100 families were given the opportunity to find out how the School delivers a values-centred education.
In excess of 400 people signed up for the Open Day which included a talk from new Head Ben Pennington who said: “I promise you that your children will have the opportunity to thrive here.”
Attendees were welcomed with music from the Worth jazz band and refreshments outside the Abbey Church before going inside to listen to Mr Pennington who spoke about how our values determine our character, how Worth means something tangible to our students and how we offer a community where everyone can thrive.
Families were then taken on tours of the School by students representing all year groups who were able to tell them about why Worth is the right place for them. The day finished with the chance to talk with academic staff.
Our next Open Day is currently in Saturday 20 March and families can book on to that day by clicking here.
We also offer private tours which can be arranged by emailing our Admissions department at admissions@worth.org.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Acknowledging our young leaders | Worth School
pageCache.text:
Your details
Acknowledging our young leaders
Congratulations to Sixth Form students who were acknowledged in assembly this week for completing the 2026 Worth Leadership Formation course.
Worth runs this course each academic year to equip young people with leadership skills to help them in their onward journeys from the School.
The course runs from September to May for Year 12 students, teaching them authentic leadership style, motivation and values. Guest speakers come to the School to speak to the students and the course is completed by attending the Saturday morning sessions, writing a reflection on the course and producing a portfolio to demonstrate service and leadership.
Students wishing to be considered for prefect positions have to complete the course but you do not have to be applying for such roles to undertake it.
At Worth, academia and results are important, but we also believe that it is through the dual focus on the highest quality education and personal exploration that young people are shaped.
Our 2026 Worth Leadership Formation cohort were congratulated in assembly this week by Head Mr Ben Pennington before gathering for a group picture.
Well done to each of them.
For more on Worth's values click here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Drama | co-curriculum and drama | Worth School
pageCache.text:
Your details
Drama
All pupils can take part in drama productions.
Although many students who join Worth already have a passion for performing, the Drama department prides itself on helping every pupil experience the power of performing and the impact that this can have on a child’s experience at school, their confidence and belief in themselves. All pupils at Worth have the opportunity to take part in large and small school productions every year and they will experience a range of different genres and styles from musicals to contemporary theatre. Most of the productions take place in the superbly equipped Performing Arts Centre and they allow students of all ages to be involved on the stage. Being part of a production at Worth is more than just an opportunity to perform, it is a chance to build new relationships, work in a team and be part of something fun, creating memories they will have for life.
Pupils are also given the opportunity to take on a backstage role, working with our Theatre Manager to learn all about technical theatre. Each production has a team of pupil technicians who take on a backstage role throughout the rehearsal period and on the evenings of the shows. Being part of the technical team is just as valued as being a member of the cast.
Worth’s own theatre workshop company provides pupils with further opportunities to explore their passion for the performing arts and take part in masterclasses which will help develop their skills to the next level.
Click here to see a panoramic view of our Performing Arts Centre theatre.
Click here to see a panoramic view of our Performing Arts Centre foyer.

Want to see Drama at Worth for yourself? Our shows for 2026-27 are Sweeney Todd, We Will Rock You and High School Musical. Tickets for any of our shows are available by clicking here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Head Master's Welcome | independent school Sussex | Worth School
pageCache.text:
Your details
Head’s Welcome
A welcome to Worth from the Head
The path of life begins at school...
Thank you for taking the time to explore our website. Here we invite you to discover what makes Worth such a distinctive and inspiring place for young people to learn, grow and flourish. Our aim is to give you a glimpse into the character, energy and opportunities that define a Worth education.
I have the enormous privilege of serving Worth as Head. My teaching career has taken me from the East End of London, GPS Sydney schools, Sherborne School in the Southwest of England, Benedictine education at Ampleforth College, choral excellence at King’s Ely School, and St Andrew’s School, Turi, in Kenya, experiences that have shaped my understanding of what education can and should be. Across very different contexts, I have seen how communities thrive when young people are challenged to work hard, encouraged to be kind and inspired to use their gifts in service of others.
Those values are personal to me too. I come from a background where you appreciate every opportunity, speak plainly, remain grounded and always look for ways to give back. These down-to-earth principles align well with the Benedictine ethos at Worth: gratitude, humility, community and a purposeful, meaningful life.
Worth understands something essential: a school is not simply a place of study; it is a place where character is formed. Here, pupils become young adults who are grounded, generous and confident in who they are, with a real desire to make a positive difference.
Worth also recognises that education must be about hard work, academic ambition and the joy of discovery – delivered within a culture where every pupil is supported and encouraged by motivated, friendly and deeply engaged teachers. Academic excellence, whatever it looks like for each individual student, is one of our highest priorities and you can be confident that our holistic education enhances, rather than compromises, academic rigour.
As a thriving school, Worth offers impressive breadth and opportunity, while remaining a place where every young person is truly known.
The true spirit of Worth, its ‘education with heart and soul’, can only be fully appreciated in person. It shines through in our service programmes, our art, music and sport, the creativity of our classrooms, our Benedictine heritage, the spiritual life of the school and the warmth of our daily interactions.
I encourage you to explore below the surface of Worth by attending one of our Open Days or booking a visit through our Admissions Department.
I look forward to welcoming you to this unique environment.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music | co-curriculum & music independent school Sussex | Worth School
pageCache.text:
Your details
Music
A balance of inclusion with excellence open to all.
The Worth Music department is a busy one and concerts and recitals happen regularly throughout the year, with the sublime acoustic of Worth Abbey providing an inspirational space for our gala concerts. The magnificent Whitehead Room provides a beautiful and intimate venue for chamber and solo concerts. Major choral services in the Abbey Church such as the Christmas Carol Service in the Autumn Term and Tenebrae in the Lent Term receive capacity congregations. House singing and Musician of the Year competitions take place each year and there are popular termly open-mic events giving rock and pop musicians a platform to perform. The department hosts masterclasses throughout the year, giving performers the opportunity to work with leading professional musicians. The department collaborates annually with the Drama department to put on a school musical. In recent years these have included Sister Act the Musical, Les Misérables, Little Shop of Horrors and Grease.
The Worth Music department is a busy one and concerts and recitals happen regularly throughout the year, with the sublime acoustic of Worth Abbey providing an inspirational space for our gala concerts. The magnificent Whitehead Room provides a beautiful and intimate venue for chamber and solo concerts. Major choral services in the Abbey Church such as the Christmas Carol Service in the Autumn Term and Tenebrae in the Lent Term receive capacity congregations. House singing and Musician of the Year competitions take place each year and there are popular termly open-mic events giving rock and pop musicians a platform to perform. The department collaborates annually with the Drama department to put on a school musical. In recent years these have included Six, The Addams Family, Sister Act, Les Misérables, Little Shop of Horrors and Grease.
Choirs
Singing is important at Worth and the school community comes together weekly to sing congregationally in services in the inspiring surroundings of Worth Abbey led by one of our choirs. A hallmark of our main school choir, the Worth Schola Cantorum, is that it is open to all without a requirement to audition but, once members, pupils are expected to be committed, inspiring loyalty, confidence and an appreciation of excellence. The most experienced singers sing by audition in our Chamber Choir. Our choirs sing at school services at Worth Abbey and annually at cathedrals both in the UK and abroad, including in recent years Westminster Cathedral and Chichester Cathedral, the Basilica of St Anthony in Padua and for a Papal Mass in St Peter’s Basilica. Singing does not just flourish in sacred music – there are also opportunities for our pupils to sing in jazz, pop and music theatre contemporary styles. Worth musicians are regularly members of the National Youth Choir of Great Britain and our alumni include several professional singers and choral conductors.
Instrumental
Instrumental musicians have a wealth of opportunities and each year the Music department adapts the instrumental and vocal groups that are on offer to take into account the strengths and interests of the pupils. Orchestral musicians can play in the 40-strong Symphony Orchestra which welcomes pupils across a range of abilities including pupils at Grade 8 standard or beyond. There are also many instrumental groups which focus on particular instrumental disciplines (such as Camerata, our string orchestra), a wealth of chamber groups (from brass to saxophone and cello groups) or pupils can form their own student-led groups which the department supports with coaching. The department also runs a Jazz Band and Concert Band which perform regularly.
Rock and pop musicians flourish through our termly ‘Live Lounge’ open mic events held in the Performing Arts Centre where they have the opportunity to perform to their peers in a supportive environment and with professional sound and lighting design. They also benefit from regular coaching sessions as a Rock Band activity.
Academic music
Classroom music is taught throughout Years 7 to 9, involving a broad mixture of listening, playing and composing in a diverse range of musical styles. The emphasis is on undertaking practical tasks as a means of learning theory, to make the course as lively and engaging as possible. Pupils regularly use music technology (Soundtrap, Noteflight, Cubase and Sibelius) and carry out composition tasks related to the areas of music studied as a means of putting the theory learned into practice and gaining valuable composing experience for the GCSE course. At A Level Worth offers courses for both Music (Eduqas) and Music Technology (Edexcel). Pupils at this level are encouraged to develop their own areas of musical interest to the highest degree, whether as performers, composers or as potential academic musicians. The use of music technology is embedded across the entire work up to and including A Level. The department has two IT suites and a recording studio with live room.
Facilities
Departmental facilities include a suite of practice rooms all equipped with modern Kawai pianos including a Kawai baby grand, a recording studio with soundproofed live room, the Coleburt Room which is the department’s main rehearsal space and a well-equipped lower school classroom, a second IT suite and a GCSE/A Level seminar room. Our practice rooms are open to students in the evenings. Kawai and Yamaha grand pianos are located in the Coleburt Room and Whitehead Room. Our main venues for concerts are Worth Abbey, the Whitehead Room and the Coleburt Room. We use the Performing Arts Centre theatre for rock and pop events, and for musical collaborations with the Drama department. Boarding houses have House pianos available for practice.
There is a wonderful amount of enthusiasm within the pupil body to make music here.

Parents’ Association
Friends of Worth is the School’s parent association.
Community and parental involvement are an integral part of school life here at Worth. The Friends of Worth plays a vital role in creating that community spirit by providing the opportunities for parents, students, teachers and the monastic community to come together and create that special environment that makes Worth so unique. It is not just the children who forge enduring friendships during their time at Worth School; this is a benefit enjoyed by their parents too.
In any school year, Friends of Worth lays on more than 20 different social events at House level, which have included activities such as a dog walk around the Worth estate, a talent evening, a quiz, curry night and many more besides.
In addition to the House events, Friends of Worth organises many and various whole school events all of which help to provide funds to purchase extras for the School which enhance the life of the pupils. Over recent years, the Friends of Worth has provided funds to equip the Robertson Fitness Suite, refurbish the Oval Pavilion adjacent to the Astropitch, to purchase hi-tech lighting for the Drama department and a cryogenic liquid nitrogen dewar for the Science department.
New parents are welcomed into the Worth community by becoming a member of Friends of Worth. The member subscription is collected via the termly bill, unless opting out.

Your details
A life full of Worth
The co-curriculum represents a substantial part of the Worth educational experience, involving a choice of more than 150 weekly activities, clubs and societies that usually take place outside the formal classroom setting.
Co-curricular activities at Worth are an essential ingredient to developing the whole person. As such we offer a large and diverse range of co-curricular activities from academic enrichment, sport, music, drama and the creative arts so that there are activities which will inspire and challenge everyone, giving the boys and girls the opportunity to learn about life in its broader context: its challenges and opportunities, and how to respond to successes and inevitable disappointments. Co-curricular activities are defined by the School’s values and pupils will recognise how their chosen activities connect with and complement their personal and spiritual development.
Co-Curriculum
With more than 150 activities, clubs and societies on offer each week, all Worth pupils are encouraged to engage and participate wholeheartedly in our extensive co-curricular programme.
Service is central to each pupil’s journey at Worth and they are encouraged to be confident that through their God-given gifts and talents they can make a positive difference to their communities and their lives through the power of service.
Worth has a large and active Duke of Edinburgh’s Award programme and we are proud to have the highest achievement rate among independent schools in the South East region.
The Arts at Worth incorporate Visual Arts, Design and Technology, and Photography, so offering exceptional opportunities for the pupils to explore and experiment in different art forms and media.
All pupils at Worth have the opportunity to take part in large and small school productions every year and they will experience a range of different genres and styles from musicals to contemporary theatre. Most of the productions take place in the superbly equipped Performing Arts Centre and they allow students of all ages to be involved on the stage.
The core philosophy of the Music department at Worth is the balance of inclusion with excellence, and the fostering of a welcoming musical community open to all. There are numerous opportunities for all to get involved in activities ranging from, for example, the Schola Cantorum to the Concert Band, from the Symphony Orchestra to live lounge rock and to performing in school musical productions.
Worth has long had a reputation for sporting excellence, with our pupils achieving representative regional and international honours, as well as Junior World Championship and European, Commonwealth and Olympic medals.
Every year pupils at Worth take part in a wide variety of trips and visits. There are many educational day trips during the school term, ranging from visits to museums and galleries to attendance at academic lectures, concerts, theatres and educational centres. A number of charitable and educational trips, and sports tours, also take place during the holidays and involve overseas travel.

pageCache.text:
Your details
The Arts
The arts at worth include visual arts, design and technology, and photography.
It’s taken studying a creative subject to develop my visual understanding of the world and it’s opened up my imagination.
The Worth Art School provides large and light studio spaces, divided into specialist areas of Visual Arts, including Fine Art, paint, print and sculpture, Design and Technology, with IT suites and workshop, and Photography, with a studio and digital facilities, and a separate darkroom.
Visual Arts
Worth’s Visual Arts department, covering Art, Craft and Design and Photography, is forward-thinking, embracing new technologies and combining them with traditional techniques. Both the working environment and teaching experience offered encourages each pupil to communicate and share their identity through the use of visual language.
Drawing underpins all creative processes at Worth and to refine this skill projects are provided to introduce pupils of all ages to a wide range of drawing techniques and media, and weekly life drawing classes are offered to Sixth Form students to learn measured academic drawing as well as other experimental drawing techniques. An additional strength is 3D sculpture and installation-based work. The pupils who choose this discipline are encouraged to make large-scale sculptures in a variety of materials using techniques such as construction, modelling and casting.
The creative atmosphere generated in the Worth art studios presents a very different learning environment for a Worth pupil and the department runs an open door policy, offering both time and space for boys and girls to explore their ideas and experiment with materials.
Click here to see a panoramic view of one of the Art studios.
Design and technology
Our expanded workshop facilities, accommodated in the Art School, include equipment such as lasers, 3D printers and a computer suite with the latest design software.
Design and Technology is a compulsory subject for all pupils in Years 7 to 9, introducing the boys and girls to a range of practical and theoretical skills and knowledge, whilst also offering an insight into potential career opportunities, such as product, graphic, interior and furniture design, architecture, engineering, computer gaming design and web design. Design and Technology GCSE is a popular choice in the expanding department, and pupils have the choice to go on studying Design and Technology at A Level.
In addition to the formal academic curriculum, students can also choose Design and Technology as a co-curricular activity, where games and design and construction challenges are combined to produce aerodynamic gliders and remote-controlled racing cars.
Click here to see the Design and Technology studio.
Photography
The Photography department has strong roots in the visual arts and design sector of school life, and is an important outlet for pupils to explore their creativity and nurture an understanding of visual literacy.
Photography is the world’s local language and thus one of the most democratic art forms widely practised. At Worth, the photography courses harness a pupil’s natural visual interest and enthusiasm and then deepen the pupil’s love, appreciation and understanding of the medium. This starts with stepping inside a camera, as pupils build their own from very basic materials and household items, and moving into practical exercises they explore and make links between darkroom processes and the tools that replicate this skill on Photoshop in a digital arena.
GCSE and A Level Photography are popular subjects but the opportunities to develop an interest in the medium are available to all pupils whether they study the subject or not. Workshops covering studio portrait photography, darkroom processing, Photoshop editing and graphics communication are popular across all years and also become a useful outlet for pupils looking to provide evidence for their Duke of Edinburgh’s Award and CAS for the IB Diploma.
Click here to see the Photography classroom.
Click here to see the Photography darkroom.

pageCache.pageTitle: History | About Us & History Independent School Sussex | Worth School
pageCache.text:
Your details
History
The origins of worth begin in 1606.
The origins of Worth lie in the foundation in 1606 of a Benedictine community at Douai, France by a group of English and Welsh monks who were in exile because of the severe penal laws in England against Catholics and, by 1617, English Catholics were sending their boys across the Channel to be educated there. In the 1790s, however, French revolutionaries plundered the Abbey and School, but the monks and boys were allowed to escape to England in February 1795. After some years sheltering on the estate of a former pupil at Acton Burnell in Shropshire, the Abbey and School finally settled at Downside in Somerset in 1814.
In the early 1930s, Abbot John Chapman established both another monastic community and a junior school in West Sussex by purchasing a country estate then known as Paddockhurst. It lay in 500 acres of landscaped grounds surrounded by woods and fields and with a view southwards over rolling countryside towards the South Downs.
The house was formerly the property of the industrialist Weetman Dickinson Pearson, later Viscount Cowdray, who in turn had purchased the estate from Robert Whitehead. Whitehead had made his fortune as the developer of the first self-propelled torpedo in the 1860s and is linked to Worth’s long connections with Austria and Germany. Whitehead’s descendants include his granddaughter the Countess Marguerite of Hoyos who married Herbert von Bismarck, the eldest son of the great Chancellor Otto von Bismarck, and his granddaughter Agathe Whitehead who was the first wife of Georg von Trapp, and the mother to his children. Captain von Trapp remarried after her death and became famous as the patriarch of the von Trapp Family Singers who were portrayed in the semi-fictional stage play and film ’The Sound of Music’.
Worth School flourished, despite being evacuated back to Somerset during the Second World War while Canadian troops were stationed in the house prior to the D-Day landings in Normandy in June 1944.
In 1957 Worth Abbey became independent from Downside and two years later in 1959 the Senior School was founded. By 1965 a Junior House for boys aged 11 to 13 had replaced the Preparatory School. In the 1990s Worth became the first English Benedictine school to take both boarding and day pupils, and the important transition to co-education began in 2008, with the first boarding and day girls accepted into the Sixth Form. Girls were welcomed into the lower years in 2010 and by September 2012 the School was fully co-educational in all years. The School has had a lay head since 2002 with the Abbot being President of the Board of Governors.
Today, Worth is a thriving school, encompassing boarding and day pupils, girls and boys.

pageCache.pageTitle: How to Apply | admissions  independent school Sussex | Worth School
pageCache.text:
Your details
How to Apply
A uniquely personal application process.
The Worth application process is uniquely personal, designed to ensure that both parents and School are able to get to know each other, and to make as informed a decision as possible.
Boys and girls join Worth either at ages 11+ (Year 7), at 13+ (Year 9) or at 16+ (Year 12). Worth also admits a small number of pupils at age 15+ (Year 11) into a one-year IGCSE/Pre-IB course, and a few places occasionally become available for boys and girls for admission at age 12+ (Year 8) or at 14+ (Year 10). Late applicants should contact the Admissions department directly.
Our Frequently Asked Questions page provides a lot of information which may help prospective families.
Age 11+ (Year 7) September 2027
Registered candidates who do not already have a CAT4 score are invited to attend an Assessment Day at Worth in November prior to their year of entry, during which they will sit the CAT4 entrance assessments.
For candidates who have already completed CAT4 testing, we will request a copy of their results directly from their current school together with a reference and they will not be required to retake the assessments.
Click here to find out more about the Admissions journey
Age 13+ (Year 9) September 2027, 2028 or 2029
Admission at 13+ is based on CAT4 assessments, which are taken either at a candidate’s current school or at Worth School. Where a candidate has already completed CAT4 testing, we will request a copy of their results together with a reference from their current school.
Click here to find out more about the Admissions journey
Age 15+ (Year 11) September 2027
Worth has a select intake at 15+ for a one-year IGCSE/Pre-IB course.
Registered candidates will be invited for an interview, either virtually or at Worth, and reports, references and predicted examination grades will be requested. Candidates will also be required to sit CAT4 assessment tests. Where a candidate has already completed CAT4 testing, we will request a copy of their results from their current school together with a reference.
Click here to find out more about the Admissions journey
Age 16+ (Year 12) September 2027
Worth has a significant intake at 16+ for either the International Baccalaureate Diploma programme or A Levels, including BTECs.
Registered candidates are invited to attend a Senior Assessment Day during the Autumn Term of their year of entry. This day includes CAT4 assessments. For candidates who have already completed CAT4 testing, we will request their results and a reference from their current school.
Overseas applicants may complete assessments remotely where appropriate, although scholarship assessments and interviews are held at Worth.
Click here to find out more about the Admissions journey
Short stays
Families can choose the schooling experience that best suits their needs – from day pupil places to full boarding (seven nights a week), as well as flexi boarding options to support busy schedules and longer commutes. We also warmly welcome international students for short stays of one or two terms, offering the opportunity to fully experience an English education within our vibrant school community. For more information click here.
Alternatively, email admissions@worth.org.uk
